critic.reason: Bit-exact and in-authority. The patch hoists the single 32-bit qh load out of the unrolled loop (shifted by 4*iqs in vec_dot_q5_0_q8_1) and derives per-iteration values in the impl as vhi = vh >> (4*i). Since arithmetic right shifts compose ((x>>a)>>b == x>>(a+b) for a+b < 32, and the maximum total shift here is 4*(iqs+vdr-1) with vdr=2, QI5_0=4, far below 32), vhi is bit-identical to the original vh[i] = qh >> (4*(iqs+i)). All eight mask/OR bit placements and both ggml_cuda_dp4a accumulations are unchanged, so the result is numerically identical; the falsifier is a pure performance question. Scope: only ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vecdotq.cuh and only the two declared symbols are touched, matching the cuda-vecdotq-v1 one-file template and the arithmetic change class. The existing call site compiles unchanged because the former array decays to the new by-value int parameter; any hidden pointer-style caller (e.g., a legacy MMQ use of the impl) would fail compilation or the 1139-case MUL_MAT correctness gate rather than pass silently, and the modern MMQ q5_0 route packs qh into tiles and uses the q8 impl. Policy: no wave-count or launch-geometry change, so it is squarely inside open hypothesis akh-v2-q5-type-specific-dequant and clear of dnr-q5-four-wave and all other DNR fingerprints. The expected_dispatch reproduces the three sealed type-6 true/true anchors (6063/57344, 4644/8192, 3096/311296; workgroup 128, LDS 1024) verbatim with the 129-call false/true tail correctly excluded, and cold_serialized load mode matches the fallback-only admission corpus. Caveat (non-blocking): the compiler likely already hoists the invariant load, so the realistic gain is limited to removed shift chains and ~2 VGPRs of array storage; effect size may land near the 0.5 percent nomination floor, which the governed exact-attribution plus graphs-on screen will adjudicate. Low-risk, well-formed first candidate for this hypothesis.
